name: Buy materials and services
summary: Buyers in the supply chain team turn approved requisitions into purchase orders and contracts for poles, cable, transformers, meters, hardware and civil, tree and construction services. Most orders are releases against multi-year agreements, a fifth need written quotes, and a few go to formal tender or sole source with committee evaluation, contractor safety checks and approval by dollar limit. The slow parts are approvals, open tender periods and supplier lead times, which for transformers grew from a few months to about a year in 2021 and 2022 and forced expediting, substitutes and deferred work.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 350,000 customers and a supply chain team of six buyers and two supervisors.
baseline.notes: Public-sector style purchasing rules (quotes and tenders by value, documented sole source) adopted as company policy by a municipally owned company; the pandemic and 2021-2022 shortages lengthened lead times.

trigger: An approved purchase requisition from stores replenishment, a capital project, fleet or operations reaches purchasing.
end_state: The purchase order or contract is issued, acknowledged and delivered (or the contractor has mobilised), or the requisition is cancelled.

volume.seasonality: More orders in late winter and spring to stock up for the construction season, and a year-end rush to commit capital budget.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate kept; consistent with about 100 orders per buyer per month, most of them agreement releases.

surge.cause: major storm restoration (emergency buys of poles, transformers, conductor and contractor crews)

evidence.note: Emergency spending above budget for poles and underground transformers in 2021 (s3); storm frequency follows the organisation file; the multiplier is the author's estimate.
Procurement team reviews suppliers and awards contracts (s1); headcount 6 in the organisation file, about 5 FTE on purchasing with the rest on supplier set-up and contract administration (estimate).
Approves stock replenishment and awards within delegated limits; share estimated.

roles.title: Vice-President (operations, engineering, customer service, finance, corporate services)

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Electronic tendering portal or bid mailbox

steps.name: ERP raises the requisition
steps.description: The ERP creates a purchase requisition, either from the overnight MRP run when a stock item falls to its reorder point or from a requester who keys a project, fleet or service need against a work order, and routes it for approval.

error.defect_description: Reorder point or quantity out of date, or wrong item code.

evidence.note: Typical ERP and MRP practice; the 60/40 split between stock and direct requisitions is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Supply supervisor approves replenishment requisitions
steps.description: The supply chain supervisor reviews the MRP replenishment suggestions in a weekly batch, adjusts quantities for planned projects and storm stock, and approves them for purchasing.

error.defect_description: Quantity too low for a coming project.

control.basis: Purchasing policy: the requester, the approver of the requisition and the buyer issuing the order are different people

steps.name: Budget holder approves the requisition
steps.description: The project manager or supervisor who owns the work order checks the item, quantity, need date and budget, and approves the requisition in the ERP or sends it back.

control.basis: Purchasing policy: the requester, the approver of the requisition and the buyer issuing the order are different people

steps.name: Buyer reviews the requisition and picks the buying route
steps.description: The buyer checks the item against the item master and approved materials list, looks for an existing standing agreement or contract, checks the estimated value against the quote and tender thresholds, and decides how to buy.

next.condition: returned to requester for missing specification
cancelled or filled from another warehouse

evidence.note: Route shares are the author's estimate for a utility that buys poles, cable, transformers, meters and hardware under multi-year agreements.

steps.name: Create a release against the standing agreement
steps.description: The buyer converts the requisition into a purchase order release at the agreed price and terms, checks the delivery address and need date and sends it to the supplier by email or EDI.

error.defect_description: Wrong price, unit of measure or ship-to.

steps.name: Request written quotes
steps.description: The buyer emails the specification and quantity to at least three registered suppliers, giving a closing date and delivery requirement, and logs the request.

control.basis: Purchasing policy: competitive written quotes between the low-value and public tender thresholds

evidence.note: Typical public-sector style quote rule; thresholds not published.

steps.name: Suppliers return quotes
steps.description: Suppliers price the request and reply with unit prices, lead times and exceptions to the terms; the buyer chases those who have not replied by the closing date.

steps.name: Evaluate quotes and select a supplier
steps.description: The buyer tabulates price, lead time and compliance with the specification, checks that each bidder is a registered supplier, and recommends the lowest compliant quote.

error.defect_description: A non-compliant item accepted on price.

steps.name: Write a sole-source justification
steps.description: The buyer and requester document why only one supplier can meet the need (proprietary relay or switchgear parts, compatibility with installed equipment, emergency), confirm the price is reasonable, and submit the justification for approval.

control.basis: Purchasing policy: documented justification for non-competitive purchases

steps.name: Draft the tender documents
steps.description: The buyer prepares the request for tender or proposal: instructions to bidders, commercial terms, pricing form, evaluation method, insurance and safety requirements, and the closing date.

error.defect_description: Evaluation criteria unclear, leading to bidder questions or addenda.

control.basis: Purchasing policy: open competitive tender above the public tender threshold

evidence.note: Separate terms for goods and services and safety requirements for contractors (s1); effort estimated.

steps.name: Requester writes the technical specification
steps.description: At the same time, the project manager or engineer writes the technical specification, scope of work, drawings and quantities, and the technical scoring criteria.

error.defect_description: Scope gaps that later become change orders.

steps.name: Issue the tender and answer bidder questions
steps.description: The buyer posts the tender, runs any bidders' meeting, answers questions in writing and issues addenda so every bidder has the same information.

steps.name: Bidders prepare and submit bids
steps.description: Suppliers and contractors prepare bids during the open period; the tender closes at the stated time and the buyer opens the bids.

steps.name: Evaluation committee scores the bids
steps.description: A committee of the requester and two technical staff scores each compliant bid against the published criteria, with the buyer checking commercial compliance and pricing, and agrees a recommendation.

error.defect_description: Scoring inconsistent with the published method.

steps.name: Check contractor safety prequalification and insurance
steps.description: For construction and maintenance services, the buyer checks in ISNetworld that the recommended contractor holds at least a C grade, and confirms insurance and WSIB clearance before award.

control.basis: Contractor health, safety and environment prequalification through ISNetworld, minimum C grade for medium- and high-risk work

next.condition: contractor must complete or improve its ISN assessment first

evidence.note: Requirement and risk levels from s1; share of contractors not yet compliant is estimated.

steps.name: Supply supervisor approves the award
steps.description: The supply chain supervisor reviews the evaluation or justification, checks that the process followed policy and that the value is within delegated limits, and approves or escalates.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: award approval limits by dollar value

steps.name: Executive approves a large award
steps.description: For awards above the supervisor's limit, the vice-president reviews the recommendation memo and approves the award, sometimes after questions to the buyer.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: award approval limits by dollar value

steps.name: Issue the purchase order or contract
steps.description: The buyer creates the purchase order or contract in the ERP from the approved award, attaches terms and specifications, sends it to the supplier and notifies unsuccessful bidders.

steps.name: Supplier acknowledges and confirms the ship date
steps.description: The supplier acknowledges the order and confirms a ship or start date; the buyer compares it with the need date on the requisition.

evidence.note: Long lead times grew in 2021-2022 (s2); shares estimated for the whole 2019-2022 period.

steps.name: Expedite or find an alternative
steps.description: The buyer asks the supplier to expedite, checks other suppliers and neighbouring utilities for stock, or proposes a substitute item to the requester, and agrees the change.

next.condition: revised date or alternate supplier accepted

evidence.note: Transformer and pole shortages and material deferrals in 2021-2022 (s2, s3).

steps.name: Chase the acknowledgement
steps.description: The buyer phones or emails the supplier about the missing acknowledgement, confirms the order was received and records the promised ship date in the ERP.

steps.name: Standards engineer approves a substitute material
steps.description: The standards engineer compares the substitute's ratings, dimensions and certification with the construction standard and the approved materials list and approves it, approves it with conditions, or rejects it.

control.basis: Approved materials list and construction standards: only approved items installed on the distribution system

steps.name: Monitor the open order
steps.description: The buyer reviews the open-order report weekly, contacts suppliers whose orders are near their due date and updates promised dates so planners know when material will arrive.

steps.name: Supplier delivers or contractor mobilises
steps.description: The supplier ships the goods to the warehouse or the contractor starts work on the agreed date; stores receiving or the project manager confirms receipt, which closes the purchasing side of the order.

evidence.note: Transformer lead times about two to three months before 2021 and about 12 months in 2022 (s2); most hardware and stock items arrive in one to three weeks (estimate). The range blends both.

exceptions.name: Lead time too long
exceptions.description: The confirmed ship date misses the need date; the buyer expedites or looks for stock elsewhere, and in about three cases in ten proposes a substitute that the standards engineer must approve.

exceptions.name: Requisition returned
exceptions.description: The buyer sends the requisition back for a missing specification or wrong item code.

exceptions.name: Contractor not prequalified
exceptions.description: The recommended contractor lacks the required ISN grade and award waits until it completes the assessment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from requisition to delivery or mobilisation
benchmarks.population: Purchase orders at a mid-size Ontario distributor, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: agreement releases are placed within days and most stock items arrive in one to four weeks; the tail reflects tenders and transformer and switchgear lead times of two to three months before 2021 and about a year in 2022 (s2).

benchmarks.population: 95 US public power utilities, August 2022 survey

pain_points.description: Long and growing lead times for transformers, switchgear and some poles in 2021-2022 meant orders had to be placed many months ahead, expedited or substituted, and some planned work was deferred.
Requisitions wait in approvers' queues and sometimes come back for missing specifications, adding days before the buyer can act.
Formal tenders take six to ten weeks end to end because specification writing, the open period and committee scoring all wait on busy engineers.

sources.title: Supply chain (suppliers and contractors page)
sources.supports: Suppliers register through an intake form reviewed by the procurement team; contracts awarded on merit with a preference for local procurement; contractors doing medium- or high-risk construction or industrial maintenance work (work near energized apparatus over 300 V, at heights of 3 m or more, excavation deeper than four feet) must hold at least a C grade in an ISNetworld health, safety and environment assessment before starting and keep it throughout, whether or not the work was competitively awarded; separate terms and conditions for goods and services; payment by EFT on agreed terms. Current page, used as a description of practice that the author assumes applied in 2019-2022.

sources.title: APPA survey of members shows distribution transformer production not meeting demand
sources.supports: August 2022 survey of 95 public power utilities: distribution transformer lead times averaged two to three months before 2021 and about 12 months in 2022 (up 429%), with some quotes over three years; most utilities had low or near-zero emergency stock; one in five projects deferred or cancelled for lack of transformers.

sources.title: Scorecard - Hydro Ottawa Limited (2017-2021) and 2021 Scorecard Management Discussion and Analysis
sources.supports: In 2021 the utility completed 92% of planned project spending, short of target because of deferrals caused by labour availability, material availability and pandemic outage restrictions; emergency spending was $8.57M against a $6.73M budget, mainly for poles and underground transformers.

assumptions: Hydro Ottawa does not publish its purchasing thresholds or delegation limits; the quote, tender and approval routes and their shares are generic public-sector style practice and tier C.
The supply chain page (s1) is current; the ISN prequalification rule is assumed to have applied in 2019-2022.
Delivery time is included so that the cycle reflects when work can start; goods receipt and put-away belong to the stores process and invoice matching to accounts payable.
The supplier lead-time range blends ordinary stock items with long-lead transformers and switchgear and the 2021-2022 shortage; a model of a single year should narrow it.

The organisation file lists only buyer and supply-supervisor on this process; requesting project managers, the standards engineer and a vice-president also take part and are added here from the organisation file's roles.
